idiom_name: typed row interfaces + Kysely query builder per table
implementation_notes: TypeScript adds compile-time column types to the JavaScript shape: a Database interface maps each table name to its row interface, and Kysely turns it into one table-typed builder - db.selectFrom('orders').selectAll().where(...).execute() resolves to Order[], the record set. The module is still plain functions (or one class holding the Kysely instance) over those typed arrays, with Drizzle's schema-first builder playing the same role, so the class-per-table structure is replaced rather than implemented. Keep the set-oriented work in the query (.update()/.delete() over a where clause) and reserve array processing for rules the database cannot express.
pitfalls: Row types are erased at runtime: a bigint or decimal column typed as number still arrives as a string from some drivers, so casting instead of parsing lies to every caller in the module.

Typed builders do not type-check raw sql`` fragments or dynamic column names - those escape hatches bypass exactly the column typing that justifies the library, and money must be summed as integer cents or a decimal type, never as JS floats.
